items.title: The d'Alembert and vakonomic motions of $z'=xy'$ differ from the same initial data
items.design_state: completed-local-counterexample; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: For L=1/2|q'|^2 and the constraint z'=x y', the d'Alembert trajectory with data (0,0,0;1,1,0) has x=t, y'=(1+t^2)^{-1/2}; if it were vakonomic for L+eta(z'-x y') then eta=0 and y''=0 would follow, contradicting the explicit y'' for t>0; the two laws differ for the same constraint and data.

references.title: D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Section 8.2 (Legendre Transformation between Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics)
D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos), Section 4.1.1 (the convexity requirement on the Legendre transform), printed pages 82-83

items.title: The ideal planar pendulum: equation of motion, conserved energy, Lyapunov stability and the frequency $\sqrt{g/l}$
items.design_state: completed-local-example; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: For the ideal planar pendulum embedded in the plane, the reduced d'Alembert equation is ml^2 theta''+mgl sin theta=0; the reduced energy is conserved; theta=0 is a strict minimum of the reduced potential and the equilibrium is Lyapunov stable; the linearised frequency is sqrt(g/l).
items.strategy: Contract the ambient equation with the tangent and identify the one-dimensional mechanical system; then invoke the energy-stability and quadratic-mode theorems.

references.title: D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Sections 3.4 (Geometrical Representations of Dynamical Motion: the plane pendulum) and 6.5 (Constrained Systems)

D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos), Section 2.3 'Constraints and Generalised Coordinates' (the simple pendulum: the equation theta-ddot = -(g/l) sin theta and the tension), printed pages 17-19

items.title: The rotating hoop: reduced Lagrangian, the equation $\theta''=\Omega^2\sin\theta\cos\theta-(g/a)\sin\theta$, and the reduced energy versus the inertial mechanical energy
items.design_state: completed-local-example; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: For the rotating carrier X(theta,t) the velocity and acceleration identities give the reduced chart with L=1/2 ma^2(v^2+Omega^2 sin^2 theta)-mga(1-cos theta); its stationary curves satisfy theta''=Omega^2 sin theta cos theta-(g/a) sin theta; the reduced energy is conserved while the inertial energy K+U changes at rate 2ma^2 Omega^2 sin theta cos theta theta'; with an ideal reaction that rate is the reaction power; and theta=0 is Lyapunov stable when a Omega^2<=g.
items.strategy: Compute the carrier kinematics, identify the reduced Lagrangian and its Euler-Lagrange equation, differentiate the two energies along solutions, and contract the ambient equation with the tangent for the reaction power.

references.title: D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos), Section 2.5.1 'Bead on a Rotating Hoop': position (2.61), kinetic energy (2.62), potential (2.63), Lagrangian (2.64), effective potential (2.65) and the equation of motion (2.66) with stationary condition (2.67), printed pages 26-27

D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Sections 7.7-7.9 (Generalized Energy and the Hamiltonian Function; Generalized energy theorem; Generalized energy and total energy)

items.title: The planar rolling disk: the holonomic constraint $x-a\theta=\mathrm{const}$ and the acceleration $f/(m+I/a^{2})$
items.design_state: completed-local-example; recorded in the batch notes
items.statement: The planar rolling disk as an ideal-constraint model (G=x-a theta, M=diag(m,I), force (f,0)): the constraint is holonomic, (m+I/a^2)x''=f with x''=f a^2/(I+ma^2), theta''=af/(I+ma^2) and multiplier lambda=-fI/(I+ma^2); for a thin disk x''=2f/(3m) and for a hoop x''=f/(2m); an explicit quadratic motion realises the acceleration.
items.strategy: Project the ideal equation onto the virtual displacement, differentiate the constraint twice, solve the linear system, and realise the motion explicitly.

references.title: D. Cline, Variational Principles in Classical Mechanics (2nd edition, University of Rochester River Campus Libraries, open textbook, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), Section 5.7 (Constrained Variational Systems: differential constraints and the straight-rolling exception) and Section 6.8 (Applications to systems involving holonomic constraints: disk rolling on an inclined plane)

D. Tong, Classical Dynamics (University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos), Section 2.3.2 'Non-Holonomic Constraints' (the rolling coin and why the general rolling constraints cannot be integrated), printed pages 20-21
